Notice that in the even dimensional case D = 2k there are two inequivalent irreducible spinor
representations (known as Weyl representations), which correspond to the Weyl spinors and can
be understood by looking at the volume element v∗= v1 · · · vD. Being v∗the product of an
even number of generators, it anticommutes with them, i.e. {v∗, va} = 0 for all a = 1, · · · , D,
but it commutes with all the elements in the even Cliﬀord subalgebra, hence with all the group
elements in Spin(V ), which implies that it must act as a scalar in the spinor representations.
This means that the inequivalent Weyl representations can be labelled by the eigenvalues of v∗.
